source_refs.note: Roman Urdu: practice long questions written from Unit 5 (PDF 142-164), not printed in the book; same questions and order as the English set. Drafts needing academic review.

blocks.text: Yeh Unit 5 (Analytical Geometry) ke poore unit se practice long questions (tafseeli sawal) hain, Board ke Section-II ke sawal ke hisse ki shakal mein: har sawal 5 number ka hai (lamba sawal, saboot (proof) ya derivation). Har sawal poore qadmon ke saath hal kiya gaya hai.

blocks.prompt:
1 Find the equation of the line through \((-1, 4)\) and \((3, -2)\). Write it in (i) general form (ii) slope-intercept form (iii) intercept form, and (iv) find its distance from the origin. (5 marks)
(\((-1, 4)\) aur \((3, -2)\) se guzarne wali line maloom karein. Ise (i) general form (ii) slope-intercept form (iii) intercept form mein likhein aur (iv) origin se iska faasla nikalein.)
blocks.explanation: Do points se slope nikalein, point-slope form lagayein, phir har form mein tarteeb dein.

book_ref.quote: then equation of straight line in two-point form is

steps: Check: dono points poore utarte hain

blocks.prompt:
2 The perpendicular from the origin to a line has length \(2\sqrt{2}\) and inclination \(135^\circ\). Find the equation of the line, its intercepts, and verify that the foot of the perpendicular lies on it. (5 marks)
(Origin se line par perpendicular ki lambai \(2\sqrt{2}\) aur inclination \(135^\circ\) hai. Line ki equation, intercepts nikalein aur dikhayein ke perpendicular ka foot (qadam) line par hai.)
blocks.explanation: \(p\) aur perpendicular ka angle diya hai: normal form \(x\cos\theta + y\sin\theta = p\) lagayein.

book_ref.quote: is the perpendicular distance of the line from the origin and

blocks.final_answer: \(x - y + 4 = 0\); intercepts \(-4\), \(4\); foot \((-2, 2)\) line par hai.

blocks.prompt:
3 Prove that the linear equation \(ax + by + c = 0\), where \(a\) and \(b\) are not both zero, always represents a straight line. (5 marks)
(Saabit karein ke linear equation \(ax + by + c = 0\) (\(a\), \(b\) dono zero nahin) hamesha straight line hoti hai.)
blocks.explanation: \(a\), \(b\) dono zero nahin, is liye sirf teen cases; har aik ko jaani pehchani line mein badlein.

book_ref.quote: represents a straight line, where

steps: Har point par \(y\) aik hi: x-axis ke parallel line
Case II, \(b = 0\): \(x = -\dfrac{c}{a}\), y-axis ke parallel line
Slope-intercept form, slope \(-\dfrac{a}{b}\), y-intercept \(-\dfrac{c}{b}\): straight line
blocks.final_answer: Saabit hua: \(ax + by + c = 0\) hamesha straight line hai.

blocks.prompt:
4 Transform \(5x - 12y + 26 = 0\) into (i) slope-intercept form (ii) two-intercept form (iii) normal form (iv) point-slope form (v) two-point form (vi) symmetric form. (5 marks)
(\(5x - 12y + 26 = 0\) ko (i) slope-intercept (ii) two-intercept (iii) normal (iv) point-slope (v) two-point (vi) symmetric form mein badlein.)
blocks.explanation: Pehle slope \(-\frac{a}{b}\) aur dono intercepts nikalein; har form inhi se banti hai.

book_ref.quote: Theorem 2: To transform the equation

blocks.prompt:
5 Prove that \(ax + by + c = 0\) can be reduced to the normal form \(\dfrac{ax + by}{\pm\sqrt{a^{2}+b^{2}}} = \dfrac{-c}{\pm\sqrt{a^{2}+b^{2}}}\), the sign being chosen so that the right side is positive. (5 marks)
(Saabit karein ke \(ax + by + c = 0\) ko normal form \(\dfrac{ax + by}{\pm\sqrt{a^{2}+b^{2}}} = \dfrac{-c}{\pm\sqrt{a^{2}+b^{2}}}\) mein laaya ja sakta hai (sign aisa ke right side positive ho).)
blocks.explanation: \(x\cos\theta + y\sin\theta = p\) se muqabla karein: aik hi line ki equations ke coefficients mutanasib hote hain.

book_ref.quote: If (i) and (iii) are identical, we must have

steps: Normal form \(x\cos\theta + y\sin\theta = p\); line \(ax + by = -c\)
Rakhne par normal form; \(p \ge 0\) is liye sign aisa ke right side positive ho
blocks.final_answer: Saabit hua: \(ax + by = -c\) ko \(\pm\sqrt{a^{2}+b^{2}}\) se taqseem karne se normal form milti hai, \(p = \dfrac{|c|}{\sqrt{a^{2}+b^{2}}}\).

blocks.prompt:
6 Transform the general equation \(ax + by + c = 0\) (\(a, b, c \neq 0\)) into (i) slope-intercept form (ii) point-slope form (iii) two-intercept form, and read off the slope and the intercepts. (5 marks)
(General equation \(ax + by + c = 0\) (\(a, b, c \neq 0\)) ko (i) slope-intercept (ii) point-slope (iii) two-intercept form mein badlein aur slope aur intercepts batayein.)
blocks.explanation: Equation ko tarteeb dein jab tak woh har standard form jaisi na ho jaaye, phir constants parhein.

book_ref.quote: Each standard form shows one property of the line at a glance

blocks.prompt:
7 Triangle \(ABC\) has vertices \(A(-4, 1)\), \(B(2, 5)\), \(C(4, -3)\). Find the equations of its three medians and show that they are concurrent. (5 marks)
(Triangle \(A(-4, 1)\), \(B(2, 5)\), \(C(4, -3)\) ki teeno medians ki equations nikalein aur dikhayein ke concurrent hain.)
blocks.explanation: Sides ke mid-points, phir har median vertex aur mid-point se; aakhir mein common point teenon mein rakh kar check.

book_ref.quote: A median joins the vertex of a triangle to the mid-point of the opposite side.

blocks.prompt:
8 For the triangle \(A(-4, 1)\), \(B(2, 5)\), \(C(4, -3)\), find the equations of the altitudes and their point of concurrency. (5 marks)
(Triangle \(A(-4, 1)\), \(B(2, 5)\), \(C(4, -3)\) ki altitudes ki equations aur un ka common point maloom karein.)
blocks.explanation: Har altitude: saamne wali side ka slope, us ka negative reciprocal, vertex se point-slope form.

book_ref.quote: An altitude is the line drawn from a vertex perpendicular to the opposite side.

blocks.prompt:
9 For the triangle \(A(-4, 1)\), \(B(2, 5)\), \(C(4, -3)\), find the right bisectors of the sides, their common point \(O\), and show that \(O\) is equidistant from the vertices. (5 marks)
(Triangle \(A(-4, 1)\), \(B(2, 5)\), \(C(4, -3)\) ke right bisectors, un ka common point \(O\) nikalein aur dikhayein ke \(O\) teenon vertices se barabar door hai.)
blocks.explanation: Har right bisector: side ke mid-point se, perpendicular slope ke saath.

book_ref.quote: A perpendicular or right bisector of a triangle is a line that is perpendicular to one side of the triangle

steps: Common point \(O\left(\dfrac{5}{7}, \dfrac{3}{7}\right)\); teesri line par bhi

blocks.prompt:
10 Prove that three non-parallel lines \(a_ix + b_iy + c_i = 0\) (\(i = 1, 2, 3\)) are concurrent iff \(\begin{vmatrix} a_1 & b_1 & c_1 \\ a_2 & b_2 & c_2 \\ a_3 & b_3 & c_3 \end{vmatrix} = 0\). (5 marks)
(Saabit karein ke teen non-parallel lines \(a_ix + b_iy + c_i = 0\) tab aur sirf tab concurrent hain jab \(\begin{vmatrix} a_1 & b_1 & c_1 \\ a_2 & b_2 & c_2 \\ a_3 & b_3 & c_3 \end{vmatrix} = 0\).)
blocks.explanation: Pehli do lines ka milaap nikalein aur teesri mein rakhein.

book_ref.quote: Theorem 3: three non-parallel lines

steps: \(a_1b_2 - a_2b_1 \neq 0\); milaap ka point \((x, y)\) Cramer's rule se
Concurrent tab jab yeh point \(\ell_3\) par ho
Yeh determinant ki teesri row ke saath expansion hai
Har qadam ulta bhi chalta hai, is liye shart zaroori aur kaafi dono
blocks.final_answer: Saabit hua: non-parallel lines concurrent hain iff coefficients ka determinant \(0\) ho.

blocks.prompt:
11 Check whether the lines \(3x + y - 7 = 0\), \(x - 2y + 7 = 0\) and \(5x - 2y + 3 = 0\) are concurrent. If so, find the point of concurrency. (5 marks)
(Check karein ke lines \(3x + y - 7 = 0\), \(x - 2y + 7 = 0\), \(5x - 2y + 3 = 0\) concurrent hain ya nahin; agar hain to point maloom karein.)
blocks.explanation: Theorem 3: coefficients ka determinant nikalein; zero ho to do lines hal karein.

book_ref.quote: the point of intersection of any two lines is the point of concurrency

steps: Slopes alag: koi do parallel nahin

blocks.prompt:
12 Find \(k\) if the lines \(2x - y + 3 = 0\), \(x + 3y - 2 = 0\) and \(kx + 4y + 6 = 0\) are concurrent, and find the point of concurrency. (5 marks)
(\(k\) maloom karein agar lines \(2x - y + 3 = 0\), \(x + 3y - 2 = 0\), \(kx + 4y + 6 = 0\) concurrent hon; point bhi nikalein.)
blocks.explanation: Coefficients ka determinant zero rakh kar k nikalein; phir pehli do lines hal karein.

book_ref.quote: set the determinant equal to zero and solve for

blocks.prompt:
13 Find the family of lines through the point of intersection of \(x - 3y + 4 = 0\) and \(2x + y - 6 = 0\). Find the member which is (a) parallel to \(4x - y + 2 = 0\) (b) perpendicular to \(4x - y + 2 = 0\). (5 marks)
(\(x - 3y + 4 = 0\) aur \(2x + y - 6 = 0\) ke intersection point se lines ki family nikalein. Woh member maloom karein jo (a) \(4x - y + 2 = 0\) ke parallel (b) us par perpendicular ho.)
blocks.explanation: \(\ell_1 + k\ell_2 = 0\) likhein, slope \(k\) mein nikalein, phir slope ki shart lagayein.

book_ref.quote: One extra condition (parallel, perpendicular, through a point) fixes

blocks.prompt:
14 Prove that the altitudes of a triangle with vertices \(A(x_1, y_1)\), \(B(x_2, y_2)\), \(C(x_3, y_3)\) are concurrent. (5 marks)
(Saabit karein ke triangle \(A(x_1, y_1)\), \(B(x_2, y_2)\), \(C(x_3, y_3)\) ki altitudes concurrent hain.)
blocks.explanation: Teenon altitudes general form mein likhein, Theorem 3 lagayein, row 2 aur 3 ko row 1 mein jama karein.

book_ref.quote: Altitudes of a triangle are concurrent.

steps: General form \(x(x_2 - x_3) + y(y_2 - y_3) + p_1 = 0\); baqi do symmetry se
Row 2, 3 ko row 1 mein jama: har column ka majmua \(0\)
Pehli row zeros: determinant \(0\); Theorem 3 se concurrent
blocks.final_answer: Saabit hua: triangle ki altitudes concurrent hain (orthocentre).

blocks.prompt:
15 Prove that the right bisectors of the sides of a triangle with vertices \(A(x_1, y_1)\), \(B(x_2, y_2)\), \(C(x_3, y_3)\) are concurrent. (5 marks)
(Saabit karein ke triangle \(A(x_1, y_1)\), \(B(x_2, y_2)\), \(C(x_3, y_3)\) ke right bisectors concurrent hain.)
blocks.explanation: Har side ka right bisector us ke mid-point se; phir Theorem 3 aur zero-row wala tareeqa.

book_ref.quote: Right bisectors of a triangle are concurrent.

steps: Right bisector general form mein, constant \(q_1\)
Symmetry se baqi do; concurrent iff determinant \(= 0\)
Row 2, 3 ko row 1 mein jama: har column \(0\)
blocks.final_answer: Saabit hua: right bisectors concurrent hain (circumcentre, teenon vertices se barabar door).

blocks.prompt:
16 Prove that the angle \(\theta\) from a line \(\ell_1\) of slope \(m_1\) to a line \(\ell_2\) of slope \(m_2\) is given by \(\tan\theta = \dfrac{m_2 - m_1}{1 + m_1m_2}\). Deduce the conditions for \(\ell_1 \parallel \ell_2\) and \(\ell_1 \perp \ell_2\). (5 marks)
(Saabit karein ke slope \(m_1\) wali \(\ell_1\) se slope \(m_2\) wali \(\ell_2\) tak angle \(\tan\theta = \dfrac{m_2 - m_1}{1 + m_1m_2}\) hai. Parallel aur perpendicular ki sharten nikalein.)
blocks.explanation: Dono lines ke inclinations \(\alpha_1\), \(\alpha_2\) aur x-axis ke saath bane triangle ka exterior angle istemal karein.

book_ref.quote: be two non-vertical lines such that they are not perpendicular to each other

blocks.final_answer: Saabit hua: \(\tan\theta = \dfrac{m_2 - m_1}{1 + m_1m_2}\); parallel \(\Leftrightarrow m_1 = m_2\), perpendicular \(\Leftrightarrow m_1m_2 = -1\).

blocks.prompt:
17 Find the interior angles of the triangle with vertices \(P(-1, 0)\), \(Q(5, 2)\), \(R(1, 6)\). (5 marks)
(Triangle \(P(-1, 0)\), \(Q(5, 2)\), \(R(1, 6)\) ke andaruni angles maloom karein.)
blocks.explanation: \(P \to Q \to R\) anticlockwise hai; har vertex par agli side se pichli side ki taraf ghoomein ('to' slope pehle).

book_ref.quote: go round the vertices anticlockwise and measure each angle

blocks.prompt:
18 The angle from the line \(y = 2x + 1\) to the line \(y = mx + 3\) is \(45^\circ\). (i) Find \(m\). (ii) Find the angle from the second line to the first, and the acute angle between them. (5 marks)
(Line \(y = 2x + 1\) se line \(y = mx + 3\) tak angle \(45^\circ\) hai. (i) \(m\) maloom karein. (ii) Doosri se pehli line tak angle aur acute angle nikalein.)
blocks.explanation: Theorem 7 mein \(\tan 45^\circ = 1\), \(m_1 = 2\), \(m_2 = m\) rakhein.

book_ref.quote: The 'to' slope comes first in the numerator.

blocks.prompt:
19 Prove that the area of the triangle with vertices \(P(x_1, y_1)\), \(Q(x_2, y_2)\), \(R(x_3, y_3)\) is \(\dfrac{1}{2}[x_1(y_2 - y_3) + x_2(y_3 - y_1) + x_3(y_1 - y_2)]\) (taking \(x_1 < x_3 < x_2\), points above the x-axis). (5 marks)
(Saabit karein ke triangle \(P(x_1, y_1)\), \(Q(x_2, y_2)\), \(R(x_3, y_3)\) ka area \(\dfrac{1}{2}[x_1(y_2 - y_3) + x_2(y_3 - y_1) + x_3(y_1 - y_2)]\) hai.)
blocks.explanation: \(PL\), \(RM\), \(QN\) perpendiculars giraayein: triangle = do trapeziums ka jama minus teesra trapezium.

book_ref.quote: A trapezium is a quadrilateral having two parallel and two non-parallel sides.

steps: Parallel sides \(y_1, y_3, y_2\); chaurai \(x_3 - x_1\), \(x_2 - x_3\), \(x_2 - x_1\)
\(x_iy_i\) wali terms cancel; chhe terms bachti hain
\(x_1, x_2, x_3\) ke hisaab se jama: formula aur determinant
blocks.final_answer: Saabit hua: \(\Delta = \dfrac{1}{2}[x_1(y_2 - y_3) + x_2(y_3 - y_1) + x_3(y_1 - y_2)]\); area \(|\Delta|\).

blocks.prompt:
20 Consider the points \(A(-2, -3)\), \(B(6, 1)\), \(C(0, 5)\). (i) Find the area of triangle \(ABC\). (ii) Find \(k\) so that \((k, 2)\), \(B\) and \(C\) are collinear. (5 marks)
(Points \(A(-2, -3)\), \(B(6, 1)\), \(C(0, 5)\) diye gaye hain. (i) Triangle \(ABC\) ka area. (ii) \(k\) maloom karein taake \((k, 2)\), \(B\), \(C\) collinear hon.)
blocks.explanation: Area formula lagayein; collinear ka matlab \(\Delta = 0\).

book_ref.quote: The converse is also true: if

blocks.prompt:
21 Prove that \(ax^{2} + 2hxy + by^{2} = 0\) (\(b \neq 0\)) represents a pair of lines through the origin which are real and distinct if \(h^{2} > ab\), coincident if \(h^{2} = ab\) and imaginary if \(h^{2} < ab\). (5 marks)
(Saabit karein ke \(ax^{2} + 2hxy + by^{2} = 0\) (\(b \neq 0\)) origin se guzarne wali do lines hai: \(h^{2} > ab\) real alag, \(h^{2} = ab\) coincident, \(h^{2} < ab\) imaginary.)
blocks.explanation: \(b\) se zarb, \(by + hx\) ka square mukammal karein, phir do squares ka farq.

book_ref.quote: represents a pair of lines through the origin. The lines are

steps: Do squares ka farq: do factors
\(h^{2} - ab\) ka sign nauiyat tay karta hai
blocks.final_answer: Saabit hua: \(by + x\left(h \pm \sqrt{h^{2}-ab}\right) = 0\); \(h^{2} >, =, < ab\) par real alag, coincident, imaginary.

blocks.prompt:
22 Find the lines represented by \(6x^{2} + xy - 2y^{2} = 0\) and the acute angle between them. (5 marks)
(\(6x^{2} + xy - 2y^{2} = 0\) se zahir lines aur un ke darmiyan acute angle maloom karein.)
blocks.explanation: \(h^{2} > ab\) check, factor, phir \(\tan\theta = \dfrac{2\sqrt{h^{2} - ab}}{a + b}\).

book_ref.quote: If the middle term splits easily, factorize (fastest).

blocks.prompt:
23 Show that the angle \(\theta\) between the lines \(ax^{2} + 2hxy + by^{2} = 0\) is given by \(\tan\theta = \dfrac{2\sqrt{h^{2} - ab}}{a + b}\). Deduce the conditions for the lines to be coincident and perpendicular. (5 marks)
(Dikhayein ke lines \(ax^{2} + 2hxy + by^{2} = 0\) ke darmiyan angle \(\tan\theta = \dfrac{2\sqrt{h^{2} - ab}}{a + b}\) hai. Coincident aur perpendicular ki sharten nikalein.)
blocks.explanation: Dono lines se slopes ka majmua aur hasil-e-zarb nikalein, phir 5.6 ka angle formula.

book_ref.quote: Thus, equation (iv) gives angle between the lines represented by equation (i).

blocks.final_answer: Saabit hua: \(\tan\theta = \dfrac{2\sqrt{h^{2} - ab}}{a + b}\); coincident iff \(h^{2} = ab\), perpendicular iff \(a + b = 0\).

blocks.prompt:
24 Find the joint equation of the lines through the origin perpendicular to the lines \(4x^{2} - 4xy - 3y^{2} = 0\). Show that the angle between the new pair equals the angle between the given pair. (5 marks)
(Origin se guzarne wali lines jo \(4x^{2} - 4xy - 3y^{2} = 0\) ki lines par perpendicular hon, un ki joint equation. Dikhayein ke dono jodon ka angle barabar hai.)
blocks.explanation: Factor karke slopes, un ke negative reciprocals, nayi lines zarb, phir formula (iv) se angles.

book_ref.quote: Perpendicular check without the formula:

steps: Naya joda: \(\tan\phi = -8\); acute angle dono mein \(\tan^{-1}8\)

blocks.prompt:
25 An aircraft flies straight from \(P(-200, 150)\) km to \(Q(400, 950)\) km. Find (i) the slope of its track (ii) the distance flown (iii) the angle of the track with the x-axis. A second aircraft flies along the track from \((0, 0)\) to \((600, 300)\) km; find (iv) the acute angle between the two tracks. (5 marks)
(Aik jahaz \(P(-200, 150)\) km se \(Q(400, 950)\) km tak seedha urta hai. (i) Track ka slope (ii) faasla (iii) x-axis se angle nikalein. Doosra jahaz \((0, 0)\) se \((600, 300)\) km tak urta hai; (iv) dono tracks ka acute angle nikalein.)
blocks.explanation: Slope aur distance formulas, phir tracks ke angle ke liye Theorem 7.

book_ref.quote: It allows us to analyze positions, distances, slopes and angles

blocks.prompt:
26 With the Sun at the origin, planet \(A\) is at \((0.6, 0.8)\) AU and planet \(B\) at \((-0.96, 0.28)\) AU. (i) Show that both are \(1\) AU from the Sun. (ii) Find \(AB\) in AU and in million km (1 AU \(\approx 149.6\) million km). (5 marks)
(Sooraj origin par hai; planet \(A\) \((0.6, 0.8)\) AU aur \(B\) \((-0.96, 0.28)\) AU par hai. (i) Dikhayein ke dono Sooraj se \(1\) AU door hain. (ii) \(AB\) AU aur million km mein nikalein.)
blocks.explanation: Distance formula AU mein, phir km mein badlein.

book_ref.quote: is a unit of length and exactly equal to 149597870700 m.
